$purpose: Canonical PRESENTATION SEMANTICS for the booking surface.
NOT loaded at runtime. NOT a source of business authority. It carries no
price, total, fee, ledger reference, Stripe object, persistence detail or
transaction semantics. Pricing authority stays in the catalog/server, payment
authority in the Postgres ledger, booking state in the Blob CAS store.
Nothing here may be imported by page or function code.
Two surface classes, deliberately NOT interchangeable:
AUTHORITATIVE — the customer-visible booking UI. Exactly one page renders
it (index.html). Assertions run against the parsed DOM of #bk-ov with
<script>, <style>, <template>, <noscript> and comment nodes removed, so a
string can only pass by being real customer-visible booking markup.
FALLBACK — the legacy inline modal kept on the hub/city pages. It is hidden
at runtime by assets/hub-booking-bridge.js and is NOT the customer-visible
source. It gets compatibility parity assertions only, and may never be used

surfaceRules.$note: Classification is DOM-structural, never a raw byte match, so a new booking page cannot escape coverage and a commented-out one cannot invent coverage.
surfaceRules.rule: A page that renders an ELEMENT with bookingRootId is a booking surface. If a real <script src> on that page resolves to bridgePath it is FALLBACK; otherwise it is AUTHORITATIVE and must be listed below.
$rule: Both halves are decided on the parsed document, never on the file's bytes.
SURFACE — EVERY published .html is parsed. There is no byte prefilter: any
textual shortcut produces false negatives on valid HTML, because
id="bk-ov" and id="bk-ov" are the same element as id="bk-ov" once
parsed. Quoting style is likewise resolved by the parser. A modal inside an
HTML comment, inside <script> text or inside <template> is not an element in
the document, so it classifies nothing.
DELEGATION — path-semantic, not basename matching. Each <script src> is
resolved the way a browser loading that page would resolve it (relative to the
page's own directory, query and fragment stripped, root-absolute honoured) and
NOT delegate, despite the identical basename;
- an off-site CDN copy does NOT delegate;
- the path in a comment or a JS string literal is not a script element, so
- on a nested page, a bare 'assets/...' src resolves under that page's own
directory and therefore does NOT delegate.

$why: Role membership is proved against live repository evidence, not merely
declared in the lists below. Disjointness and union say nothing about which
page belongs to which role — swapping template-city.html with a real public
hub page would satisfy both and still be wrong.
sitemap        the file that advertises pages to customers. Every public
surface must appear in it; the template must not.
templateConsumer  the generator, read-only. Its template input IS the
template role; no public page may be that input.
Swapping the two roles fails both signals at once.
roleEvidence.$rootDocument: sitemap.xml advertises the authoritative surface as the bare site root, so an empty pathname maps to this file.

surfaceRules.$stepTabs: The step tabs are read from this container in physical DOM order. Looking each tabId up individually would impose the manifest's own order on the result, so a physical swap of two tabs would compare equal and pass.
surfaceRules.$publishRoot: netlify.toml sets publish = ".", so every .html under the repo root is served, at any depth. Discovery therefore walks recursively; a root-only readdir let a nested page such as cities/boston-hub.html ship outside the guard.
$scanExcludedDirs: Structural exclusions only — each is a directory that by ROLE cannot hold an
authored public page, never a list of known page names:
node_modules  dependency tree (also gitignored, so never deployed)
netlify       server-side root; netlify.toml declares functions = 'netlify/functions'
shared        shared modules, not a document root
tests         the test tree, including this suite's own scratch fixtures
docs artifacts reports archive   documentation and audit output
Entries are matched against the path RELATIVE TO THE PUBLISH ROOT, so only the
top-level directory of that role is skipped — a nested 'cities/tests/' is still
assets/ is deliberately NOT excluded: it is served, so a booking page placed

surfaces.$counts: 1 authoritative + 11 public fallback = 12 runtime/public HTML surfaces, plus 1 non-runtime template.
surfaces.$paths: Entries are paths relative to the publish root, POSIX-separated. All current surfaces sit at the root; a nested surface would be listed as e.g. 'cities/boston-hub.html'.

$anchoredText: Every entry is ANCHORED: `anchor` is resolved inside the parsed #bk-ov DOM and
must match exactly as many elements as `texts` has entries, compared in document
order. This replaces whole-modal substring containment, under which a decoy such

as
Card on File Required
could satisfy the
contract while the real element drifted.
Why anchoring rather than computed visibility: the booking modal is a wizard.
Inactive steps and the .pay-choice-desc panels are display:none until the
customer reaches them, so they ARE customer-visible copy. Requiring computed
visibility would delete real coverage. Anchoring closes the decoy hole without
that cost: a decoy that does not match the anchor is ignored, and one that does
match changes the element count and fails.
match: 'exact'    normalised text of the element equals the expected string
match: 'contains' normalised text of the element contains the expected string,
used where the element legitimately carries extra copy.
$visibility: STRUCTURAL VISIBILITY — an explicit, deliberately limited contract.
By default every element an anchor resolves to must be free of structural
hidden markers, on itself or on any ancestor inside #bk-ov:
hidden               attribute
aria-hidden="true"   attribute
display:none         INLINE style
visibility:hidden    INLINE style
Required customer-facing copy therefore cannot be satisfied by markup that is
hidden in one of those four ways.
WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is not browser computed style. Visibility driven by an
external stylesheet or by a class — including anything that hides #bk-ov
itself until the modal opens — is NOT modelled here and remains a
browser-preview concern. Do not read a pass as proof that a customer can see
the text; read it as proof that the markup is not hidden in a way the markup
itself declares.
EXEMPTIONS. Progressive disclosure is legitimate, so an entry may list
visibility.exemptIndices — the element positions allowed to be hidden — with
visibility.revealedBy naming the control that reveals them. The revealedBy
selector must actually render, so an exemption cannot be claimed for markup
nothing can reveal. The declared exemptions must EXACTLY equal the set of
elements that are really hidden: a stale exemption fails just as loudly as an
undeclared hidden element.
